children.text: Harbor of the Mother Oak’s Blessing
Nestled on Barlop’s winding canal just south of the Refu Forest,

caters to merchants, hunters, and wayward travelers seeking passage, supplies, or safe harbor. Its weathered docks creak under lantern light, and the air smells of tar, fish, and forest moss. Elven lanterns and driftwood totems carved with forest runes offer a hint of the woodland spirits’ protection over the vessels moored here.
Medium Humanoid (elf), Neutral good • Dockmistress of Tide’s Edge
Tall and lithe, with sea-green hair braided with kelp and wooden beads. Her pale skin bears faint runic tattoos of waves and leaves.

Born in the shadow of Refu’s oldest oaks, Elara left her family’s grove to learn the ways of the tidal trade. Over decades she mastered navigation, negotiation, and a bit of forest lore—enough to advise travelers which river trails to avoid when dusk falls.
Elara adds +2 to Acrobatics and Stealth checks.
Advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can’t put her to sleep.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 1d8+3 piercing damage.
Over twenty years ago she negotiated the marina’s founding treaty between Barlop fishers and Refu Forest rangers.
Losing her dock to forest fires
She once spared a river spirit hunter for promising to guard her boats.
Fishermen’s nets vanish mysteriously by night. Elara seeks discreet help to trail the culprit into the forest shadows.
Medium Humanoid (dwarf), Lawful neutral • Boatwright and Dockhand Foreman
Stout and broad-shouldered, with a braided beard streaked by salt and oil. His arms bear burn and hammer scars.
A third-generation boatwright whose family has built vessels for Barlop’s traders since before the canal’s opening. Rorik prides himself on sturdy hulls and seaworthy craftsmanship.
Advantage on saving throws against poison, and resistance to poison damage.
Adds double proficiency bonus to checks with smith’s tools.
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d8+2 bludgeoning damage.
Once freed a trapped water spirit by repairing its overturned barge.
A malformed hull capsizing in storm waters
Keeps a hidden workshop under the docks.
Rorik needs rare driftwood logs from Refu’s flooded trails. He seeks escorts to retrieve them before forest spirits claim the wood.
Simple wooden rod with linen line and iron hook.
30-foot diameter, capable of holding Medium creature if it fails a DC 10 Dex save.
Good for mooring and rigging; water-resistant.
Burns for 6 hours on a flask of oil; protected from spray.
Heavy canvas; used for patching sails or making tarps.
Hollow cork ring with hemp rope, floats for up to 300 lb.
Seats up to two Medium creatures.
Hull patching, cleat replacement; full overhaul priced individually.
Secured slip under Tide’s Edge lanterns.
Experienced deckhand; can handle rope and oar.
A glass vial of bright red liquid.
As an action, drink to regain 2d4+2 hit points.
Rumored to have first been brewed by Refu Forest druids who revered the Mother Oak’s restorative sap.

opened sixty years ago when Barlop’s merchants petitioned forest wardens to bless a safe canal through the Refu’s swampy tail. Since then, travelers pass beneath wind-whispering oaks carved with warding runes. Locals say that at night, the forest spirits step onto the docks to inspect each boat, ensuring no harm comes to their woods.”
